body:
A `solve` working session died of a **V8 heap OOM inside Hive Mind's own log sanitizer**, ~10 minutes *after* the AI tool had finished successfully and pushed all its work. Three separate defects turned a clean, recoverable situation into a dead session that was never continued.

## The incident

| | |
|---|---|
| Command | `solve https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1069 --think xhigh --tool codex --attach-logs --verbose` |
| `$` execution UUID | `0ea1c630-cfdf-477e-8528-29d175a7fe64` |
| `$` session name | `dd1acfbe-3c01-4ffa-8c78-f825457f5813` |
| Tool session id | `01a05c1c-0c3d-7472-a431-11d9c948e162` |
| Image | `konard/hive-mind-dind:2.15.1` |
| Exit | **139** (SIGSEGV), `oomKilled=false` |
| Log (private) | https://github.com/konard/private-logs/tree/main/log-tmp-start-command-logs-isolation-docker-0ea1c630-cfdf-477e-8528-29d175a7fe64 |

Timeline:

```
13:04:12Z  last commit + push  ->  d2f3d702e..03c90e68a  HEAD -> issue-1069-05d4ea1feb9b
13:56:31Z  agent's final read-only verify: working_tree_entries=0, head == origin head
13:57:00Z  codex session closes
13:57:07Z  hive-mind: "No uncommitted changes found"; PR #1070 converted draft -> ready
13:57 ->   --attach-logs: read 134 MB log, sanitize, escape, sanitize AGAIN
14:07:47Z  FATAL ERROR: Reached heap limit - JavaScript heap out of memory  -> SIGSEGV
```

No work was lost (everything was already pushed), but the session was killed and never resumed.

---

## 1. A killed session is only *offered* for resume, never resumed

```
[VERBOSE] session-resume: last tool session id in ... is 01a05c1c-0c3d-7472-a431-11d9c948e162 (scanned 1 chunk)
[VERBOSE] Session dd1acfbe-... was killed; offering resume from last session 01a05c1c-...
[VERBOSE] Session dd1acfbe-... kill reporting: killed=true recovered=false cause=forced-kill policy=report
```

`src/session-monitor.lib.mjs:831` — Hive Mind correctly recovered the tool session id from the log, then stopped at *offering*. `recovered=false`, `policy=report`. Nothing continued the work.

**Expected:** the bot should **initiate** the resume itself, with context preserved, so the session continues on its own — ideally re-entering **the same `$` session id / container** rather than starting a fresh isolated run. A crash in a post-processing step is exactly the case that should auto-continue without a human pressing a button.

Worse, the offer was not even timely: the crash was at **14:07:49Z**, but the bot only noticed at **20:14:00Z** — over 6 hours later — because the *bot itself* had been restarted in between and only re-detected the finished session on startup. Which leads to:

**Expected:** on startup the bot should **resume all still-running / interrupted commands**, so a bot restart never orphans in-flight work. (`src/bot-lifecycle.lib.mjs:103` already has a "Failed to resume tracked sessions" path — it needs to actually cover killed sessions with a recoverable tool session id.)

## 2. V8 heap OOM is misclassified as `forced-kill`

```
[VERBOSE] kill-diagnostics: cgroup oom=0 oom_kill=0, mem available=9.1 GB/11.7 GB, victims=0
[VERBOSE] kill-diagnostics: cause=forced-kill — forced kill — memory (10.3 GB of 11.7 GB RAM available (12.2% used)), disk /: 104.4 GB free of 192.7 GB (45.8% used)
```

The diagnosis is "plenty of memory, must have been a forced kill". In reality the process died of memory exhaustion — just at the **V8 heap limit (~2.1 GB)**, not at the cgroup limit. `docker inspect` `oomKilled=false` and `cgroup oom_kill=0` are both *technically correct*; they simply cannot see a V8 self-abort. Classifying on those signals alone yields a false negative for "out of memory" every single time Node hits its own heap cap.

The evidence was sitting in the very log that was being scanned:

```
FATAL ERROR: Reached heap limit Allocation failed - JavaScript heap out of memory
12: 0x15385ff v8::internal::Runtime_RegExpExecMultiple(int, unsigned long*, v8::internal::Isolate*)
```

The repo already knows this string — `src/child-exit.lib.mjs:9,34` documents it for SIGABRT — but `src/session-kill-diagnostics.lib.mjs` (cause selection at lines 271-281) never consults the log.

**Expected:** `KILL_CAUSE_OUT_OF_MEMORY` when the log tail contains `FATAL ERROR: Reached heap limit` / `JavaScript heap out of memory`, regardless of cgroup counters. Exit 139/134 plus that marker is unambiguous. The recovery message and the resume policy both depend on this classification being right.

## 3. The sanitizer buffers the entire log in memory (this is what OOM'd)

`src/github.lib.mjs:440`:

```js
const rawLogContent = await fs.readFile(logFile, 'utf8');
```

A 134 MB log becomes one JS string, and the pipeline then makes several more full-size copies:

- `sanitizeLogContent(rawLogContent)` — full copy
- `escapeCodeBlocksInLog()` = `logContent.replace(/```/g, ...)` (`src/github.lib.mjs:28`, called at `:449`) — another full copy
- `src/token-sanitization.lib.mjs:819-828` — a global regex `/(?:^|[\s:=])([a-f0-9]{40})(?=[\s\n]|$)/gm` driven in a `while (exec(...))` loop with a `hexReplacements[]` accumulator, plus `String.replace` with a global pattern over the whole 134 MB

`Runtime_RegExpExecMultiple` in the crash stack is precisely that last step. Default old-space is ~2 GB; several 134 MB strings plus the match arrays blow through it — while the box had **10.3 GB free**.

It also does the work **twice**. The log shows `Sanitized 591 secrets` once for the inline-comment path and again for the `gh-upload-log` path:

```
📁 Large log file (148MB), will use gh-upload-log
🔍 Sanitizing log content to mask GitHub tokens...
🔒 Sanitized 591 secrets ...
🔧 Escaping code blocks in log content for safe embedding...
📁 Log file too large for inline comment (148MB), using gh-upload-log
🔒 Sanitized 591 secrets ...      <-- again
```

The size check at `src/github.lib.mjs:580` happens *after* the whole file was already read, sanitized and escaped for a comment that was never going to be posted.

**Expected:**
- Decide the upload strategy from `logStats.size` **before** reading anything.
- Sanitize as a **stream** (line- or chunk-oriented, with a small overlap window so tokens spanning a chunk boundary are still caught), writing to a temp file — never materialising the log, or any transform of it, as a single string.
- Never sanitize the same content twice.
- More generally: **no unbounded buffering anywhere in Hive Mind.** Log capture, session monitoring and comment building should all be memory-bounded, so no Hive Mind code path can leak or grow with log size. A worker with a bounded heap for the sanitize step would also contain any residual blow-up instead of taking the whole run down.

## Impact

The AI tool did its job perfectly, pushed a green PR, and the *reporting* step killed the run and left it unrecovered for 6 hours. The kill was then reported to the user as a mysterious "forced kill" on a machine with 10 GB free.

Related: #1493 (resource leaks), #2134 (better handling of killed task), #2015 (false positives/negatives on killed sessions), #744.
title: Killed session is only offered for resume, never resumed; V8 heap OOM misclassified as forced-kill; log sanitizer buffers the whole log in memory
